newsitem.title: USA: Schools say no losses from Mercury Finance.
newsitem.headline: Schools say no losses from Mercury Finance.

text.p: Officials from school groups in Illinois and Michigan said Friday that funds they sponsored through Cadre Financial Services Inc. have suffered no losses as a result of investments in troubled Mercury Finance Co commercial paper.

Jerry Glaub, a spokesman for the Illinois Association of School Boards, said the more then 400 schools and community colleges that invested in Cadre-run funds would not see any loss from Mercury Finance holdings.
Cadre is a unit of AMBAC Inc.
A memo sent to fund participants Friday by the school board group and Cadre said the Illinois School District Liquid Asset Fund Plus no longer had any Mercury Finance holdings.

The memo said the holdings were a permissible investment for the fund and that Cadre "working in conjuction with the fund's board of trustees was able to arrange for the sale of this commercial paper at no loss to the fund."
Glaub said he believed the commercial paper was sold after news hit last week about Mercury Finance's financial situation.

Mercury, a Lake Forest, Ill., consumer finance company, restated its last four year's earnings lower by a total of about $90 million after discovering accounting discrepancies. The company later said it was in default on its short-term lending agreements.
The company has also been served with a Federal Bureau of Investigation search warrant seeking financial documents.

Jerry Keidel, executive director of the Michigan Association of School Administrators, said that it was his understanding that none of the schools that had invested in the funds suffered any losses. He added that only a "very small" portion of the $1.3 billion investment portfolio run by Cadre for Michigan schools contained Mercury Finance commercial paper.

Officials at Cadre were not available to comment. In a statement Friday, AMBAC confirmed the sale of the Mercury Finance commercial paper and that the two state funds incurred no losses as a result of the sale. A spokesman for the bond insurer declined to comment on details of the sale.
